title: Operator Benchmark Signal Contract
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the canonical signal contract that operator-facing benchmarking and diagnostic tooling must publish and consume. The goal is to make benchmark outputs, live probe signals, and debug dumps interoperable across the runtime, scheduler, and operator tools (canary harness, chaos, capacity planner) so we can automate analysis, alerts, and regression detection.

Scope:
- Operator-facing artifacts produced by the benchmarking harness, in-situ probes, and debug collectors.
- Signal schema, retention/TTL guidance, sampling guarantees, and minimal metadata.
- Validation checks and examples for reporters and consumers.

Who should use this page: SREs running capacity experiments, runtime engineers adding probes, platform tool authors, and performance analysts.

Signal contract summary

High level: every published record is a single line JSON document (NDJSON) or equivalent record in our time-series/trace store. The minimal fields below are mandatory for all operator benchmark events. Variants (sampled traces, kernel telemetry) append auxiliary sections per the field rules.

Mandatory fields (every event):
1. record_id (string): stable UUID for the event.
2. timestamp (ISO8601 string): event generation time in UTC.
3. origin (string): source component, one of: "benchmark-harness", "kernel-agent", "scheduler", "kv-prefetch", "grpc-proxy".
4. env (string): environment tag, e.g., "staging", "prod-us-west-2", "dev-local".
5. signal_type (string): short descriptor, see Signal taxonomy below.
6. sample_weight (string): decimal string representing the inverse probability weight (e.g., "1.0" for unsampled).
7. schema_version (string): contract version, current: "v1.2".
8. payload (string): JSON-encoded string containing signal-specific fields (see section).

Signal taxonomy (recommended values for signal_type)
- benchmark_invocation: end-to-end benchmark run metadata + aggregated metrics
- micro_op: short (<500ms) kernel or op-level measurement
- latency_histogram: histogram bucket summary for an endpoint/route
- trace_span: sampled distributed trace snippet (open-telemetry compatible)
- kernel_profile: compacted kernel counters / timings for hot path slice
- failure_annotation: structured failure signal with error class and remediation hints
- resource_snapshot: periodic GPU/host memory and temperature snapshot

Payload contract: examples and required subfields
- benchmark_invocation payload must include:
  - run_id (string)
  - model_name (string) and model_variant (string)
  - route (string) (e.g., /v1/generate)
  - duration_ms (number as string)
  - total_tokens (number as string)
  - p50,p90,p95,p99 (strings) – latency percentiles in ms
  - cpu_peak_pct, gpu_util_peak_pct (strings)
  - config_blob (string): base64 of the harness config used

- micro_op payload must include:
  - op_id (string)
  - kernel_hint (string) optional but recommended (e.g., "fused-attention-v3")
  - duration_us (string)
  - gpu_id (string) if applicable
  - tags (string): comma-separated lightweight tags for grouping

- latency_histogram payload must include RFC-compliant histogram buckets (text table) and a cardinality estimate field. Example: 
  "buckets": "[\"0-1ms:102\", \"1-4ms:523\", \"4-16ms:130\"]", "cardinality": "755"

- trace_span payload: must be OTLP-compatible base64-encoded protobuf or a JSON snippet including service, span_id, parent_span_id, start_ns, duration_ns, and annotations array.

Sampling and sample_weight rules
- Deterministic sampling: a benchmark harness must deterministically sample using run_id + seed so replays generate the same sampled set.
- Minimum unsampled fraction: for every 10k events, at least 10 must be unsampled (sample_weight="1.0") to enable precise small-variance estimators.
- Sample_weight encodes the inverse sampling probability. Consumers multiply observed metrics by sample_weight to recover unbiased estimators.

Retention, TTL and storage targets
- Short-lived probe events (micro_op, kernel_profile): TTL = 14 days in the raw blob store, compressed aggregated summaries kept for 90 days.
- Benchmark_invocation and latency_histogram: TTL = 365 days (retained for capacity planning and regression hunting).
- Failure_annotation: TTL = 3 years (retained for audit and long-tail incident analysis).
- Operators must include `retention_policy` in the payload when deviating from defaults with explicit business justification and reviewer approval.

Validation and automated checks (CI for reporters)
1. Schema validation: every reporter should run `bench-signal-validate` (open-source tool) against the generated NDJSON before ingestion.
2. Cardinality sanity: histogram cardinality must match sum of buckets within ±1% tolerance.
3. Weight and sampling checks: sampled sets must report effective sample rate and at least one seed-consistent unsampled record per 10k events.
4. Checksum: payload must include payload_checksum (sha256 hex string) to detect on-wire corruption.

Example NDJSON record (one line, pretty shown here):
{
  "record_id": "2a5a8f3c-99b1-4d80-ae47-d5d9c7c078e4",
  "timestamp": "2026-11-15T18:32:12Z",
  "origin": "benchmark-harness",
  "env": "staging-us-east-1",
  "signal_type": "benchmark_invocation",
  "sample_weight": "1.0",
  "schema_version": "v1.2",
  "payload": "{\"run_id\":\"run-20261115-7\",\"model_name\":\"redwood-7b-q\",\"model_variant\":\"q8_0\",\"route\":\"/v1/chat/completions\",\"duration_ms\":\"12345\",\"total_tokens\":\"4567\",\"p50\":\"12.3\",\"p95\":\"48.9\",\"cpu_peak_pct\":\"12.1\",\"gpu_util_peak_pct\":\"78.3\"}"
}

Reporter implementation guidance
- Language SDKs: provide `bench-reporter` libraries in Python and Go. SDKs should expose helpers: `start_run()`, `emit_micro_op()`, `emit_histogram()`, `finish_run()` and `flush()` for graceful shutdown.
- Backpressure: reporters must implement a bounded async queue with default depth 200 and drop oldest-on-overflow policy. Dropped events must emit a lightweight counter metric `bench.reporter.dropped` with reason tags.
- Retry semantics: use idempotent publish with at-most-once delivery preferred for ephemeral micro_op events; benchmark_invocation should be retried until ACKed with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts.

Operator dashboards and alerts (consumers)
- Must map signal_type -> dashboard panel via the `origin` tag. Example alert rules: 
  - p95(latency_histogram) > 300ms for 5m -> page SRE-PAGE, severity=high.
  - micro_op duration_us increases >3x baseline for a kernel_hint -> create performance-investigation ticket.

Schema evolution policy
1. Backward compatible additive changes allowed in minor versions (v1.x -> v1.y).
2. Breaking changes require bumping major schema (v2.0) and migration plan published 30 days before enforcement.
3. Consumer teams should ignore unknown fields and log if more than 3% of incoming records contain unexpected top-level keys.

Diagnostic playbook: how to use these signals to investigate a latency regression
1. Reproduce: run the benchmark-harness with the same run_id and seed.
2. Collect: emit micro_op and kernel_profile samples at 1% deterministic sampling for the affected route.
3. Correlate: join micro_op op_id to kernel_profile via record_id references and GPU timestamps.
4. Isolate: check resource_snapshot for thermal throttling or memory pressure.
5. Confirm: re-run with kernel-level debug logging enabled and compare p95 delta.
6. Rollback criteria: if regression > 2x p95 and kernel profile shows increased instruction counts, rollback kernel or model variant.

Checklist for adding a new reporter or signal
1. Open PR: include schema docs and example NDJSON.
2. Add tests: unit test for `bench-signal-validate` and an integration test that posts to ingest staging endpoint.
3. Add counter metrics for dropped events and payload_checksum failures.
4. Register signal in the central registry (link in related_pages).
5. Request privacy review if payload contains any user-identifiable metadata.

Operational examples and CLI
- Validate file: `bench-signal-validate --schema v1.2 ./my-run.ndjson`
- Publish locally (staging): `bench-reporter publish --file ./my-run.ndjson --env staging-us-east-1`
- Quick histogram inspect: `jq -r '.payload | fromjson | .p95' < my-run.ndjson | stats`

Ownership and escalation
- Owner: eng-serving-runtime / Performance instrumentation subteam (oncall roster in team wiki).
- Review cadence: signal contract reviewed quarterly and after any major runtime/kernel release.
- Escalation path: performance incident -> runtime oncall -> scheduler lead -> product owner for model variant.

Appendix A: compact config table (defaults)
| Field | Default | Rationale |
| retention_policy.micro_op | 14d | Limits high-cardinality raw storage |
| retention_policy.benchmark_invocation | 365d | Needed for regressions and capacity history |
| sampling.min_unsampled_rate | 0.001 | One unsampled per ~1000 events to keep low-variance checks |
| reporter.queue_depth | 200 | Keeps memory bounded under stress |

Appendix B: minimal reporter JSON schema (pseudo)
{
  "record_id": "string",
  "timestamp": "string",
  "origin": "string",
  "env": "string",
  "signal_type": "string",
  "sample_weight": "string",
  "schema_version": "string",
  "payload": "string",
  "payload_checksum": "string"
}

Notes and references
- See related guides for synthetic workload signatures and harness config knobs (links in related_pages).
- This contract is intentionally pragmatic: compact, NDJSON-first, and compatible with both TSDB ingestion and object-store archival.
